_meta: Corrections of slips of the copy in data/corpus/op_translit.json (D-177; used by tools/build_op_signs.ts, checked by tests/lang.test.ts). The corpus is carved as it stands except for these words. Each entry: the text, the word as the copy prints it (pieces joined by | where a line breaks it), the reading carved (same pieces), how many times it occurs, and its evidence, which the build and the tests verify: 'ario' = the corrected signs are exactly Kent's rules on Schmitt's reading of the same word (ARIo), i.e. the two editions agree and only the copy differs; 'copy' = the corrected word stands, so spelled, elsewhere in the corpus; 'convention' = the copy's form cannot occur in Kent's convention (a doubled consonant letter: the script writes no gemination) and the correction only undoubles it. A difference of reading between Kent and Schmitt is NOT corrected here (the corpus is carved; research/OP_SIGNS.md and Q-288 list them).

corrections.why: a stray h: the king's name has no ha sign (xa-ša-ya-a-ra-ša-a-ma, Schmitt's Xšayaṛšām); the copy spells the name without it everywhere else
a stray length mark: Haxāmanišiya (ha-xa-a-…), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling in every other text
a stray i before y: xa-ša-a-ya-θa-i-ya-ha-ya-a as Schmitt's xšāyaθiyahyā and as the copy spells the word in the other XP texts
p for t: the conjunction utā (u-ta-a), Schmitt's reading, and the copy's spelling everywhere else
the accusative būmim (ba-u-mi-i-ma), Schmitt's reading and the copy's own spelling in DNa line 1-2 and the XP texts
v for y: tya-šām (ta-ya-ša-a-ma), Schmitt's tayašām
a stray i: adāraya (a-da-a-ra-ya), Schmitt's reading and the copy's own spelling of the verb in DNa
n for m: the accusative gāθum (ga-a-θa-u-ma), Schmitt's reading
a stray i: vināθayatiy (vi-i-na-a-θa-ya-ta-i-ya), Schmitt's vināθayati
s for š: vināθayaiš, Schmitt's vināθayai̯š and the copy's own spelling two words later
a lost length mark: utā (u-ta-a), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling everywhere else
a doubled n, which Kent's convention never writes (the script writes no gemination): xšnutam
the genitive the phrase needs ('in the house of king Darius'): Dārayavahauš (da-a-ra-ya-va-ha-u-ša), Schmitt's reading; the nominative is a slip of the copy
the logogram XŠ with its complement -hyā, as the copy writes the same word in XPc and XPi (XŠhyâ); lower case xšhyâ would spell xa-ša-ha-ya-a, no Old Persian word
a lost length mark: Auramazdā (…-za-da-a), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling everywhere else
a lost i: xšāyaθiya (xa-ša-a-ya-θa-i-ya), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling 39 times elsewhere
a lost length mark: Dārayavauš (da-a-ra-…), Schmitt's reading and the copy's spelling everywhere else
